Real small capitals, and the two that do not exist

Nothing here comes from the mathematical block. Small caps is assembled from characters that linguists needed: Latin letter small capital forms scattered across IPA Extensions, Phonetic Extensions and Latin Extended-D, each encoded to write a particular sound rather than to make a tidy alphabet. Two of them were never encoded at all. There is no small capital q and no small capital x anywhere in Unicode, so those two letters stay ordinary lowercase and you can see the join.

Because these are ordinary letters from the main plane, combining marks sit on them properly, so an underline or a strikethrough behaves the way you would expect, which is not true of the mathematical alphabets. Type in capitals and they pass straight through untouched, being capital-shaped already. The overall effect is understated enough for section labels on a link page or a byline, where script or blackletter would be far too much.

Also searched as: small caps generator, small text generator, tiny caps copy and paste.

Where Small Caps text works, and where it does not

WorksReads as ordinary text everywhere, because these are normal Unicode letters rather than a maths alphabet. Watch outUnicode has no character for every letter in this style, so the missing ones stay plain. That is the honest fallback, not a fault.

Small Caps questions

Why are q and x still lowercase?

Because the characters do not exist. The small capital letters were added piecemeal for phonetic notation, and no phonetic alphabet ever needed a small capital q or x, so neither was encoded. Rather than leave a blank, this site keeps the plain lowercase letter, which is the least jarring of the available options.

What happens if I type in capitals?

They come out unchanged. A small capital is already the shape of a capital, only shorter, so there is nothing to convert an uppercase letter into. If you want the classic look, type the first letter of a word in capitals and the rest lowercase, and you get a full-height initial followed by small capitals.

Can I add an underline or strikethrough to small caps?

Yes, and this is the one style here where that works dependably. These characters live in the same plane as ordinary letters, so combining marks attach and render as intended. The mathematical alphabets frequently place those same marks badly, which is why crossed-out or underlined text is best built on this set.
